key: rendering::aray lays its whole beam in one frame and bray persists
lesson: Correction of an earlier assumption: an ARAY beam is NOT too fast to photograph. ARAY's Update traces the entire line and creates every BRAY point in a single frame (ARAY.cpp:70-211), and BRAY lives 30 frames by default, or 1020 if the same line is re-sparked over itself (BRAY.cpp:45, ARAY.cpp:110-122). The beam fires out of the face OPPOSITE the spark (nxi = rx*-1, ARAY.cpp:70). BRAY only fills cells that are empty, so a beam that appears missing means the path was obstructed or the spark never arrived with life==3 -- check the optical path, not the shutter speed. Note ARAY never creates PHOT; it creates BRAY, which is coloured by FILT through the same wavelength code photons use.
title: ARAY lays its whole beam in one frame and BRAY persists

The one exception: sparking NBLE converts it to PLSM with ctype=PT_NBLE (SPRK.cpp:117-129), and that plasma REVERTS to NBLE at end of life instead of dying (FIRE.cpp:66-71). So the only persistent glowing plasma is a bed of NBLE on a circuit that re-sparks it. NBLE is PROP_CONDUCTS, which is what makes this work.
title: Only NBLE-sourced plasma is self-sustaining

lesson: LN2's source file is LNTG.cpp, not LN2.cpp. It spawns at 70.15K (LNTG.cpp:29), freezes to NICE at 63K and, critically, its HighTemperatureTransition at 77K is PT_NONE -- it is simply deleted with no visible byproduct (LNTG.cpp:39-42), which is why it appears to vanish rather than boil. Particle-to-particle heat conduction is unconditional and is NOT gated by the ambient-heat flag (Simulation.cpp:2466-2509), so contact with any room-temperature matter pushes it past 77K almost immediately. Setting cell temperature does nothing because ambient heat defaults off. Keep it away from warm neighbours or re-set each particle's temp.
title: LN2 is LNTG and dies by deletion at 77K

evidence: Renderer.cpp review explaining why some 'glowing' choices read as flat pixels in captures.
key: rendering::default render preset downgrades pmode_glow
lesson: The default preset is RENDER_BASC|RENDER_FIRE|RENDER_SPRK|RENDER_EFFE, which does not include PMODE_GLOW; render_parts downgrades an unsatisfied PMODE_GLOW to a flat PMODE_BLEND pixel (Renderer.cpp:361-372). Visible bloom in the default view therefore comes only from the FIRE_ADD/FIRE_BLEND fire-buffer path. When picking a material to make something look like it is glowing, check that its graphics function sets a FIRE_* bit, not just PMODE_GLOW. FIRE and LAVA always contribute and are the loudest; LCRY sets no glow bits at all and never blooms.
title: Default render preset downgrades PMODE_GLOW

key: rendering::deco alpha 255 fully replaces an element colour
lesson: The deco blend is colr = (deca*decr + (256-deca)*colr) >> 8 with deca incremented to 256 at full alpha (Renderer.cpp:427-444), so alpha 255 is an exact replacement. Two caveats: decoration is skipped entirely in Heat, Life-gradient, Basic and Destructibility display modes, and elements flagged NO_DECO (LCRY always, PHOT unless FLAG_PHOTDECO) cannot be decorated. Decoration also never tints the fire-buffer bloom unless the element sets DECO_FIRE, which only LIGH does -- so decorating FIRE has no visible effect at all.
title: Deco alpha 255 fully replaces an element colour

It has neither PROP_LIFE_DEC nor PROP_LIFE_KILL (DEUT.cpp:37) so its life never decays on its own, its HighTemperature is effectively 10000K so it has no heat transition, and it spawns near ambient so it radiates nothing. Once life reaches 240 its graphics function unconditionally sets PMODE_GLOW|FIRE_ADD (DEUT.cpp:150-157). Seal it behind a wall box and keep it compressed. PLSM cannot do this and GLOW only brightens under pressure or turbulence.
title: Packed DEUT is the stable non-destructive light source

lesson: DEUT.cpp update(): particle field `life` = concentration. Per-tick maxlife = ((10000/(temp+1))-1) * (5 - 8/(gravtot+2)), gravtot = |gravOut.forceX|+|forceY| at that cell (Newtonian self-gravity magnitude; enable via sim.newtonianGravity(true), separate from ambient GRAV_VERTICAL/OFF/RADIAL mode). Colder temp -> higher maxlife ceiling; more local self-gravity -> up to 5x multiplier vs 1x at zero gravity. life<maxlife: DEUT cannibalizes 1/3-chance adjacent DEUT (absorbs life+1, kills neighbor) to concentrate. life>=maxlife: spawns new low-life DEUT into empty neighbors to dilute. This is the real compression mechanic, not scripted.
title: DEUT life=concentration, maxlife formula

Without refueling the reactor pulses once and dies. FSN-2 lesson applies: 'Fuel depot with plug valves' is in the playbook Scale-up section for exactly this reason.
title: One-shot tokamak fusion burns through fixed DEUT fuel and stops

evidence: v6 script: for angle=0,315,45 do for r=131,67 do ... end end — both loops ran the outer but inner executed 0 times because 131 > 67 with default +1 step.
key: workflow::lua for-loop descending requires explicit step=-1
lesson: Lua for-loop: `for r=131,67 do` loops ZERO times because start > end and default step is +1. Must use `for r=131,67,-1` for descending loops. Lost hours in v6 build placing 0 PCLN because I tried to iterate `for r=131,67` which never executed.
title: Lua for-loop descending requires explicit step=-1

evidence: v6 build had INWR ring at r=132, WIFI at (476,143), gap of ~45 pixels diagonal between them. Build looked complete but no SPRK appeared because the spark path was broken.
key: workflow::check inwr ring continuity before declaring wire complete
lesson: When placing INWR ring at specific radius, check after each segment that the ring connects back to itself AND to other conductors. My v6 had INWR ring at r=132 around torus but the wire from WIFI at (478,143) couldn't reach it because no diagonal connector existed. INWR is wire (conducts across gaps) but doesn't conduct without continuous pixel path.
title: Check INWR ring continuity before declaring wire complete

key: workflow::pcall's second return value is dropped inside an and/or expression
title: pcall's second return value is dropped inside an and/or expression
lesson: `local ok, val = cond and pcall(f, x) or false` silently loses the real second return of pcall: embedding a multi-return call inside a boolean and/or chain truncates it to ONE value (Lua only keeps every return of a call when it's the LAST expression in an assignment/call list, not when it's an operand of `and`/`or`). Result: `val` is always nil and any `type(val)=='table'` check silently fails forever, with no error raised. Fix: split it -- `local ok, val; if cond then ok, val = pcall(f, x) end`.
evidence: rpg.lua's self-updater: `local ok3, releases = ok2 and body and pcall(json.parse, body) or false` meant `releases` was always nil, so the GitHub-releases changelog feature silently never detected any update for a full test cycle before this was caught by tracing the logic line by line.

key: workflow::http.get/http.post require an interface-event call stack
title: http.get/http.post require an interface-event call stack
lesson: TPT's Lua http.get/http.post call AssertInterfaceEvent() internally and throw 'this functionality is restricted to interface events' when called outside one. event.TICK/KeyPress/KeyRelease/MouseDown/MouseUp/MouseWheel handlers all carry eventTraitInterface (GameControllerEvents.h) so calling http.* from inside onTick/onKeyDown etc. works fine -- but calling it directly through the net.listen HTTP bridge's executeLua action does NOT, since that handler runs outside the normal event dispatch. Any bridge-based test of an http.get/http.post-calling function must trigger it via a real boot/tick/key path (e.g. restart the process and let onTick call it naturally) and then only use the bridge to read back state afterward -- never call the http-touching function directly through the bridge.
evidence: Confirmed via direct bridge test: `pcall(http.get, url, headers)` through executeLua returned `ok=false, err='this functionality is restricted to interface events'`, while the exact same call succeeds when it runs inside rpg.lua's onTick-driven R.checkForUpdate().

key: workflow::github api endpoints need a user-agent header or return 403
title: GitHub API endpoints need a User-Agent header or return 403
lesson: api.github.com rejects requests with no User-Agent header. Always pass `{{'User-Agent','<anything>'}}` as the headers table to http.get when hitting GitHub's REST API from TPT Lua.
evidence: Confirmed via curl before wiring it into rpg.lua's update checker.

key: workflow::any onmouse*/onwheel handler must gate on r.tptmenus symmetrically
title: Any onMouse*/onWheel handler must gate on R.tptMenus symmetrically
lesson: In rpg.lua's sandbox/TPT-menu toggle (R.tptMenus), every one of onMouseDown, onMouseUp, and onWheel independently swallows native TPT input unless it explicitly bails with `if R.tptMenus then return end` at the top, BEFORE it sets any R.mouse.*/zoom/hotbar state. Fixing onMouseDown alone left onMouseUp still unconditionally clearing R.mouse.l/r and returning false, which meant native TPT never saw the button go back up and kept painting/dragging as if it were still held. Treat these three handlers (plus tpt.hud(0) at boot, which independently hides the whole toolbar including the stamp-browse button regardless of R.tptMenus unless R.setTptMenus also calls tpt.hud) as ONE bypass surface -- fixing one without auditing the others reintroduces the same bug from a different angle.
evidence: Three separate bug reports this session (place doesn't work -> stuck holding down -> wheel brush-size doesn't work -> stamp browser unreachable) were four instances of the same missing-bypass pattern in onMouseDown, onMouseUp, onWheel, and the tpt.hud(0) boot call.

key: workflow::set the github default branch to the active feature branch for a fork's landing page
title: Set the GitHub default branch to the active feature branch for a fork's landing page
lesson: When a fork's real work lives on a non-default branch (e.g. rpg-and-realism) and `master` just mirrors upstream untouched, the repo's front page still shows master's README by default -- making a heavily modified fork look untouched to anyone visiting the GitHub URL. `gh repo edit <repo> --default-branch <branch>` fixes this in one call and is safe for a personal single-maintainer fork.
evidence: Applied to phoenixfire808/The-Powder-Toy, default branch -> rpg-and-realism.
